figure: FIGURE A.3 — in-figure annotation vs. drawn year markers
issue: The figure's own annotation claims a precision convention it does not apply: "approximate era markers (≈), not release dates", yet no bar carries an "≈" glyph — the years are printed bare (2017, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2024, 2025, 2025, 2026). The caption's "The dates are approximate era markers, not release dates" is therefore carried by prose alone, and the "(≈)" in the annotation points at a convention that is absent from the drawing.
evidence: Rendered page 454 annotation: "Selected illustrative mechanism milestones — a non-comprehensive chronology; approximate era markers (≈), not release dates. [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]". Bar markers as printed: 2017, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2024, 2025, 2025, 2026 — no approximation glyph on any of them.
acceptance_test: Either prefix each year marker with "≈" (e.g. "≈2017") or change the annotation to "approximate era markers, not release dates" and delete the unused "(≈)". Acceptance: the figure and its caption use the same approximation convention, and no reader can mistake a marker for a release date.

figure: FIGURE A.4 — legend
issue: The system-side / model-side distinction is encoded by hue alone in the legend ("blue = system-side · green = model-side"). In grayscale the two families collapse to similar mid-tones; the only non-hue cues are the rotated SYSTEM / MODEL labels at the left and an unexplained lightness jump at the blue/green boundary. The legend does not tell the reader that the left-hand labels carry the family distinction, so a grayscale reader is left to infer it.
evidence: Rendered page 456: legend line "blue = system-side · green = model-side · within each family, shade = further from the weights is darker". Five system-side bands are blue (navy at top through pale blue at bottom); three model-side bands are green (dark green at top through pale green at bottom). The only non-color family markers are the rotated "SYSTEM" and "MODEL" labels beside the vertical arrow.
acceptance_test: Add a non-hue cue for family membership — e.g. a bracket or group label per family, or a hatch on the model-side bands — and state in the legend that family membership is also marked by the SYSTEM / MODEL brackets. Acceptance: the figure is unambiguous in a grayscale proof, with no reliance on hue to separate the two families.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — DeepSeek rows, scope cells
issue: The reporting date "reported 2026-06" appears only in the KV-cache scope cell of each DeepSeek row; the compute scope cell carries no date. The date therefore reads as a property of the KV metric alone, although the source line attributes both ratios to the same source (arXiv 2606.19348). The GLM row has the same asymmetry ("reported 2026-08" in the KV cell only).
evidence: Rendered page 451, DeepSeek V4-Flash row: KV cell "reported 2026-06 single-token KV cache"; Compute cell "single-token inference FLOPS" (no date). GLM-5.3-Flash row: KV cell "reported 2026-08 per-layer KV (BF16)"; Compute cell "attention only per head / layer" (no date). Source line: "DeepSeek V4: arXiv 2606.19348."
acceptance_test: Move the reporting date to the row level (e.g. under the model name) or repeat it in the compute scope cell, so both metrics in a row carry the same date. Acceptance: no metric in the table can be read as undated, and the printed date matches the YYMM of the cited arXiv identifier.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — caption, cross-reference
issue: The caption directs the reader to "the paragraph above beginning 'Same message as Fig 7.1's GQA line'". Because FIGURE A.2 sits at the top of printed p. 451, that paragraph is on the preceding page, so "above" is not resolvable from the figure's own page and the reader must hunt for it.
evidence: Rendered page 451 shows the figure occupying the top of the page with the caption below it; no paragraph beginning "Same message as Fig 7.1's GQA line" appears on this page.
acceptance_test: Replace "the paragraph above" with an explicit pointer (e.g. "the paragraph on p. 450 beginning ..."). Acceptance: the quoted opening words are verified to occur at the referenced location, and the pointer resolves without a page-flip guess.

figure: FIGURE A.2 — red warning box
issue: The box warns only that the rows are not a cross-model performance ranking. It does not warn that a FLOP ratio is not a latency ratio, which is the most likely misreading of the compute column ("100%→~10%", "100%→~27%", "100%→~33%") — a reader may infer a proportional speedup. The book's own argument elsewhere separates FLOPs from latency, so the figure should carry the same guard rather than relying on the reader to remember it.
evidence: Rendered page 451, box text: "NOT A CROSS-MODEL PERFORMANCE RANKING / Each row is relative to that model's OWN stated baseline — no shared scale". Compute column values: "100%→~10%" (DeepSeek V4-Flash), "100%→~27%" (DeepSeek V4-Pro), "100%→~33%" (GLM-5.3-Flash), with scope "single-token inference FLOPS" and "attention only per head / layer".
acceptance_test: Extend the box or the footnote with one clause (e.g. "a FLOP ratio is not a latency ratio") and confirm the caption repeats the guard. Acceptance: the figure contains no wording from which a reader can derive a latency or throughput claim from the compute column.

figure: FIGURE 6.2 — 'Latency distribution: the mean hides the tail'
issue: The red hatched region is labelled '1% stragglers (> 5 s cross the SLO)'. The straggler cluster is AT 5.0 s, not above 5 s, per the prose ('a 1% straggler cluster at 5.0 s') and the figure's own box ('population p99 = 5.0 s'). The parenthetical reads as a claim that the stragglers exceed 5 s, which is false and also inconsistent with the drawn region, which is centred on 5.0 s and straddles it.
evidence: Prose, printed p. 98: 'the body of requests follows a log-normal distribution centered near 0.8 s (99% of observations), with a 1% straggler cluster at 5.0 s'. The hatched band in the figure spans roughly 4.5-5.5 s, i.e. centred on 5.0 s. The label's '> 5 s' is therefore both wrong and inconsistent with the geometry it labels.
acceptance_test: Change the label to '1% stragglers (cluster at 5.0 s, past the 2 s SLO)' or equivalent; assert that no annotation in the figure states a strict inequality that the drawn geometry contradicts.

figure: FIGURE 6.2 — 'Latency distribution: the mean hides the tail'
issue: The 2 s line is labelled in the figure as 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)' but the caption calls the same line the '2 s request-latency line' and explains that request-latency violations are a superset of TTFT violations. Labelling the line '(TTFT budget)' invites exactly the conflation the caption is written to prevent, and the caption's phrase 'the p95 SLO is met' adds a third characterisation of the same line.
evidence: Figure label: 'SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)'. Caption: 'while 1% of requests exceed the 2 s request-latency line - a superset of TTFT violations, and a tail a p99 SLO does not surface' and 'the light band shades the full SLO-violating region (> 2 s)'. The caption's own logic (request latency >= TTFT, so request-latency violations are a superset) is incompatible with the figure's parenthetical, which names the line a TTFT budget.
acceptance_test: Relabel the line 'SLO 2 s (request latency)' and add a one-line note in the figure or caption stating 'TTFT <= request latency, so TTFT violations are a subset of this region'. Assert that the string 'TTFT budget' does not appear attached to the 2 s line.

figure: FIGURE 6.2 — 'Latency distribution: the mean hides the tail'
issue: The p90 (0.94 s) and p95 (0.99 s) reference lines are 0.05 s apart on an axis spanning 0-6 s. At print size this is roughly 2-3 pt of separation, so the two dashed lines are effectively coincident and only the offset text labels distinguish them. The figure's whole argument is about reading percentiles off the distribution, so the percentile markers must be individually resolvable.
evidence: Axis range 0-6 s across a plot roughly 4.5 in wide at print size; 0.05 s therefore occupies about 0.037 in (2.7 pt). The p50 (0.80), p90 (0.94) and p95 (0.99) markers are all crowded into the left 17% of the axis, while the histogram body itself occupies only ~0.4-1.6 s.
acceptance_test: Either add a zoomed inset over 0.7-1.1 s showing the p50/p90/p95 markers, or replace the three separate lines with a single annotated percentile ladder (e.g. a small table or a bracket with 'p50 0.80 | p90 0.94 | p95 0.99') so that no two markers are closer than 6 pt at print size.

figure: FIGURE 7.5 — 'KV cache size vs context, by attention geometry (full-MHA vs GQA)'
issue: The annotation '9.5K max context (32K in ~500 GB)' contains a quantity (~500 GB) that is not derivable from any curve, reference line, or legend entry in the figure, and the parenthetical's referent is never stated. The reader is left to guess whether 500 GB is a KV pool, a total residency, or a hardware capacity.
evidence: Curves and lines in the figure: full-MHA FP16 at 32K = 2.62 x 32,000 = 84 GB; full-MHA FP8 at 32K = 42 GB; GQA FP16 at 32K = 10.5 GB (or 5.1 GB on the plotted 0.16 curve); '8xH100 raw (640 GB)'; 'KV budget ~436 GB'. None yields ~500 GB. The caption explains the 9.5K figure ('~24.9 GB at 9.5K (total weights+KV residency then ~165 GB, 7.1)') but says nothing about 500 GB. The vertical 9.5K guide also appears to run the full plot height rather than terminating at the constraint it marks, so it reads as a generic x-position rather than a limit.
acceptance_test: State the referent of '~500 GB' in the annotation (e.g. '8xH100 raw 640 GB minus 140 GB weights') and make it arithmetically derivable from the figure's own numbers, or delete it. Terminate the 9.5K vertical guide at the curve/constraint it marks and label that constraint.

figure: FIGURE 7.5 — 'KV cache size vs context, by attention geometry (full-MHA vs GQA)'
issue: The right-hand annotation block ('FP16 full-MHA at 128K = 335 GB / FP8 full-MHA at 128K = 168 GB / GQA FP16 at 128K = 21 GB ...') is set in small type directly over the plotted region, where it sits on top of gridlines and the flat '8xH100 raw (640 GB)' line, and it is the only place the reader can find the 128K values. The block is also the location of the FIG-7.5-01 error, which is easy to miss at this size.
evidence: The three-line annotation block occupies the upper-right of the axes, overlapping the 640 GB reference line and the log grid; its type is visibly smaller than the axis tick labels. The 335 GB and 168 GB values are correct (2.62 x 128,000 = 335 GB; 1.31 x 128,000 = 168 GB), so the block is worth keeping but must be legible and correct.
acceptance_test: Move the 128K value block outside the axes (e.g. as a small table beneath the legend, or in the caption), set it at no less than the axis-label size, and assert that no annotation text overlaps a plotted line or gridline.

figure: FIGURE 7.2 — 'History recurrence and attention history have different lifetimes'
issue: The caption states 'the KV row is cumulative (snapshot 3 retains KV1+KV3)', but the figure's third snapshot shows KV1, KV2 and KV3. The caption's parenthetical contradicts the drawn content and would, if read literally, assert that KV2 is discarded.
evidence: Figure, bottom row: the third group contains three boxes labelled KV1, KV2, KV3, captioned '3 cached tokens'. Caption: 'the KV row is cumulative (snapshot 3 retains KV1+KV3)'. The figure's own sub-label '3 cached tokens' and the caption's word 'cumulative' both indicate KV1+KV2+KV3.
acceptance_test: Change the caption to '(snapshot 3 retains KV1+KV2+KV3)'. Add a caption/figure cross-check that every token identifier named in a caption appears in the corresponding drawn group.

figure: FIGURE 7.2 — 'History recurrence and attention history have different lifetimes'
issue: The figure draws three equal-weight state boxes ('state after t1', 'state after t2', 'state after t3') side by side, which visually implies that three recurrent states are held simultaneously. The caption and the figure's own note both assert the opposite ('recurrent snapshots are successive, not jointly retained'). The drawn geometry therefore permits exactly the wrong inference, and the correction is carried only by a small note.
evidence: Top row: three identically styled pink boxes labelled 'state after t1 / fixed-size state', 'state after t2 / ...', 'state after t3 / ...'. Bottom row: the KV boxes are cumulative and grow (1, 2, 3 boxes), so the two rows are visually parallel in weight even though their lifetimes differ. The figure's note 'Arrows = token input / state flow; snapshots are schematic' and the caption's 'successive, not jointly retained' are the only signals that the earlier states are overwritten.
acceptance_test: Make the visual encoding carry the claim: fade or outline the superseded state boxes (t1, t2) and keep only the latest filled, or stack the snapshots with an explicit 'overwritten' marker on the earlier ones. Assert that the number of visually solid state boxes equals the number of retained states (one).

figure: FIGURE 7.4 — 'Four-bit values, different scale bills'
issue: The caption and the figure subtitle both assert that bar widths are proportional to bytes ('Payload and local-scale bar widths are proportional to bytes'; 'Bar widths are proportional to bytes and local-scale bytes only'), but the scale segments - the entire point of the figure - appear to be drawn wider than their byte share, and the two bars appear to be drawn to equal total width despite representing 17 B and 18 B. If a minimum-width rule was used to keep the scale segments visible, the proportionality claim is false exactly where it matters.
evidence: MXFP4 bar: light payload segment (16 B) spans roughly 335 px and the dark scale segment (1 B) roughly 25 px, i.e. about 21 px/B. NVFP4 bar: two light segments (8 B each) span roughly 145 px each (about 18 px/B) and the dark '2 B scales' segment spans roughly 70 px, i.e. about 35 px/B - roughly twice the byte-proportional width. Both bars appear to span the same total x-range although they represent 17 B and 18 B (a 5.9% difference that should be visible on a common scale).
acceptance_test: Measure the rendered segment widths and assert the ratios 16:1 (MXFP4) and 8:8:2 (NVFP4) within 5%, and that the NVFP4 bar is 5.9% longer than the MXFP4 bar. If a minimum-width rule is required for legibility, replace the proportionality claim with an explicit scale break or a note that the scale segments are drawn at minimum width, and move the byte counts into the labels (which already carry them).

figure: FIGURE 7.6 — 'Memory floor: inference vs fine-tuning (canonical 70B, FP16 unless noted)'
issue: The figure asserts '~5 GB over 2xH100' for the inference bar, but the y-axis spans 0-1400 GB, so a 5 GB difference between the bar top (165 GB) and the 160 GB reference line is about 0.36% of the axis height - roughly one pixel at print size. The claim is therefore not verifiable from the chart, and the bar top and the 2xH100 line are visually indistinguishable.
evidence: Y-axis ticks run 0, 200, 400 ... 1400 GB. Inference bar labelled '~165 GB'; legend line '2xH100 (160 GB)'. 165 - 160 = 5 GB = 0.36% of the 1400 GB axis. The annotation '~5 GB over 2xH100' is the only carrier of this fact.
acceptance_test: Add a zoomed inset or a broken axis for the inference bar region so that the 160 GB and 165 GB levels are visually separable, or replace the annotation with an explicit statement that the overshoot is below the chart's resolution and give the numbers in the caption.

figure: FIGURE 7.1 — 'Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)'
issue: The boxed note '8 query heads : 1 KV head (x 8 groups)' is inconsistent with the drawing, which shows three groups (three K/V boxes) with an ellipsis. The parenthetical '(x 8 groups)' is ambiguous: it reads either as 'the canonical model has 8 KV-head groups' (64 query heads total) or as 'the ratio is multiplied by 8', and neither reading is what the picture shows.
evidence: Figure: three groups of eight blue query-head glyphs, each fanning into one orange 'K/V' box, followed by an ellipsis on both rows. Boxed note: '8 query heads : 1 KV head (x 8 groups)'. Caption: 'the load-bearing number is the n_q : n_kv ratio (8 : 1 here) - 8 query heads share one KV head, so the per-token KV falls x8'.
acceptance_test: Make the count explicit and consistent with the drawing, e.g. '8 query heads : 1 KV head (3 of 8 groups shown)' or '64 query heads : 8 KV heads (8 groups of 8)'. Assert that the group count named in the note matches the number of groups drawn or is explicitly marked as elided.

figure: FIGURE 6.2 — 'Latency distribution: the mean hides the tail'
issue: Grayscale distinguishability of the percentile markers is weak: p50 is a green dashed line and p90/p95 are blue dashed lines, which in grayscale differ mainly in a small luminance step, and the p90/p95 pair is already nearly coincident (see FIG-6.2-04). The SLO line is blue dash-dot, so the only reliably distinguishable pair in grayscale is p50 versus the rest.
evidence: Marker styles in the figure: p50 green dashed; p90 and p95 blue dashed; SLO 2 s blue dash-dot; sample p99 red dashed. The histogram bars are blue-filled. In grayscale, green and blue dashed lines of the same weight are hard to separate, and the blue histogram fill competes with the blue reference lines.
acceptance_test: Assign distinct dash patterns (e.g. solid / dashed / dash-dot / dotted) to p50, p90, p95 and the SLO so that all four are separable in grayscale, and confirm by rendering the page to grayscale and checking that each marker is uniquely identifiable.

figure: FIGURE 7.4 — 'Four-bit values, different scale bills'
issue: Unit wording: both local lines read '= 4.25 bit/value' and '= 4.5 bit/value'. The unit is a count of bits per value and should be plural ('bits/value'), consistent with the book's other per-token units.
evidence: Figure text: 'Local: 17 B / 32 = 0.53125 B/value = 4.25 bit/value' and 'Local: 18 B / 32 = 0.5625 B/value = 4.5 bit/value'. The arithmetic is correct (17/32 = 0.53125 B = 4.25 bits; 18/32 = 0.5625 B = 4.5 bits).
acceptance_test: Change 'bit/value' to 'bits/value' in both lines; grep the manuscript for 'bit/value' and normalise.

figure: FIGURE 7.4 — 'Four-bit values, different scale bills'
issue: Label placement is inconsistent between the two bars: payload labels ('32 E2M1 values = 16 B', '16 values = 8 B') sit inside the bar, while the scale labels ('1 B scale', '2 B scales') sit below and outside it. The reader must move the eye between two different label positions to compare the two rows, and the scale labels are the ones that carry the figure's actual message.
evidence: MXFP4 bar: '32 E2M1 values = 16 B' centred inside the light segment; '1 B scale' printed below the bar at its right end. NVFP4 bar: '16 values = 8 B' inside each light segment; '2 B scales' printed below the bar at its right end.
acceptance_test: Place all segment labels inside their segments (or all outside) consistently, and ensure the scale-segment labels remain legible if the segment is narrow.

figure: FIGURE 7.2 — 'History recurrence and attention history have different lifetimes'
issue: Caption grammar: 'a recurrent layer group updates hidden state, fixed-shape state' is a comma splice and is missing an article; the intended meaning is that the recurrent group updates a hidden state which is fixed-shape.
evidence: Caption: 'a recurrent layer group updates hidden state, fixed-shape state, while a separate full-attention group retains growing KV history'. The figure's own box text reads 'state after t1 / fixed-size state', which is the clearer phrasing.
acceptance_test: Rewrite as 'a recurrent layer group updates a hidden state - a fixed-size state - while a separate full-attention group retains a growing KV history', and align the terminology ('fixed-size state' in the figure vs 'fixed-shape state' in the caption) with the book's glossary entry for recurrent state.

figure: FIGURE 7.1 — 'Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)'
issue: The figure's internal annotations ('many query heads -> few shared KV heads', 'query heads', 'shared KV heads', and the boxed '8 query heads : 1 KV head (x 8 groups)') are set noticeably smaller than the figure title and smaller than the caption text, and appear to fall below the 8 pt print floor for figure in-text annotations. This was measured by eye on a ~68 dpi rendering, so it must be confirmed against the source.
evidence: Relative type sizes on the rendered page: figure title is clearly the largest; the subtitle and the three coloured labels plus the boxed note are roughly 60-70% of the caption's size. The house convention sets an 8 pt floor for figure in-text annotations.
acceptance_test: Measure the rendered font size of every string inside the figure (subtitle, 'query heads', 'shared KV heads', boxed note) and confirm each is >= 8 pt at print size; enlarge if not. Note that this check is an estimate from a downscaled render and must be repeated on the print-resolution PDF.
